questions.q: Let $A \left(a, b\right), B  \left($3, 4\right)$ and  \left(-6, - 8\right)$ respectively denote the centroid, circumcentre and orthocentre of a triangle. Then, the distance of the point $P  \left(2a + 3, 7b + 5\right)$ from the line $2x + 3y - 4 = 0$ measured parallel to the line $x - 2y - 1 = 0 is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $A \left(a, b\right), B \left($3, 4\right), $C\left(-$6, - 8\right)$ denotes centroid, circumcentre and orthocentre respectively.

We know that, the line joining orthocentre and circumcentre is divided by centroid in the ratio $2: 1$, where distance from orthocentre being the larger part.

$⇒ a = $\dfrac{2 \times 3 + 1\left(- 6\right)}{2 + 1},$b = $\dfrac{2 \times 4 + 1 \left(-8\right)}$${2 + 1}$

$⇒ a = 0, b = 0$

$⇒ P ≡ \left($2 \times0 + 3, 7 \times0 + 5\right)$

$⇒ P ≡ \left($3, 5\right)$

Distance from $P$ measured along $x - 2y - 1 = 0$

$⇒ x = 3 + $rcos\theta,$y = 5 + $rsin\theta

Where, tan\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}

So, the distance of point from $2x + 3y - 4 = 0$ will be,

2\left($3 + $rcos\theta\right) +3\left($5 + $rsin\theta\right) -$4 = 0$

$⇒ $r\lleft(2cos\theta +$+3sin\theta) = -17$

$⇒ r = \left|-$-17\left(2 \cdot \dfrac{2}{5} +3 \cdot \dfrac{1}{5}\right)\right|$

$⇒ r = \left|\dfrac{- 17\sqrt{5}}{7}\right|$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{17\sqrt{5}}{7}$

$

questions.q: A point on the straight line, $3x + 5y = 15$ which is equidistant from the coordinate axes will lie only in:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let \left(a, a\right)$ be a point on the line $3x + 5y = 15$

$⇒ 3a + 5a = 15$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{15}{8}$

$∴$ Point is \left(\dfrac{15}{8}, \dfrac{15}{8}\right)$ which lies in ${1}^{st}$ quadrant

Again, Let \left(- a, a\right)$ be a point on the line

~ ~ $3x + 5y = 15$

$⇒ - 3a + 5a = 15$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{15}{2}$

$∴$ Point is \left(- \dfrac{15}{2}, \dfrac{15}{2}\right)$ which lies in ${2}^{nd}$ quadrant

Hence, required point lies in${1}^{st}$~and~${2}^{nd}$ & quadrants.

questions.q: The distance between the two points& $A$ and $A^{'}$~which lie on $y = 2$~such that both the line segments $AB$~and $A^{'}B$~(where $B$~is the point  \left(2, 3\right)$) subtend angle $\dfrac{π}{4}$& at the origin, is equal to$

questions.solution:
Let the slope of $OB$~be~${m}_{1} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

and the slope of~$OA$~be~${m}_{2} = \dfrac{2}{x}$

Now angle between two lines,~$tan\dfrac{π}{4} = \left|\dfrac{\dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{2}{x}}{1 + \dfrac{6}{2x}}\right|$

i.e.~\left|\dfrac{\dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{2}{x}}{1 + \dfrac{6}{2x}}\right| = 1 ⇒ \left|$\dfrac{3x - 4}{2x + 6}\right| =$1$

$3x - 4 = \pm \left(2x + 6\right)$

$⇒ {x}_{1} = 10, {x}_{2} = - $\dfrac{2}{5}

$⇒ AA^{'} = 10 + \dfrac{2}{5} = \dfrac{52}{5}$

questions.q: If $p$ and $q$ are the lengths of the perpendiculars from the origin on the lines, $x cosec \alpha - ysec\alpha = kcot2\alpha$ and $xsin\alpha + ycos\alpha = ksin2\alpha$ respectively, then $k^{2}$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
${L}_{1}: x cosec \alpha - ysec\alpha = kcot2\alpha$
$\dfrac{x}{sin\alpha} - \dfrac{y}{cos\alpha} = k\dfrac{\cos 2\alpha}{\sin 2\alpha}$

$\dfrac{xcos\alpha - ysin\alpha}{sin\alpha cos\alpha} = k\dfrac{\cos 2\alpha}{2sin\alpha cos\alpha}$
$⇒ xcos\alpha - ysin\alpha = \dfrac{k}{2}\cos 2\alpha$

We know that Perpendicular distance from a point~ \left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)$to~$ax + by + c = 0$~is~\left|\dfrac{a{x}_{1} + b{y}_{1} + c}{a^{2} + b^{2}}\right|$

Perpendicular distance from $( 0, 0 )$ is $p = \left|\dfrac{0 - 0 - \dfrac{k}{2}\cos 2\alpha}{\cos^{2}\alpha + \sin^{2}\alpha}\right|$

$⇒ p^{2} = \dfrac{k2}{4}\cos^{2}2\alpha$

${L}_{2}: xsin\alpha + ycos\alpha - ksin2\alpha = 0$

Perpendicular distance from $( 0, 0 )$ is $q = \left|\dfrac{0 + 0 - ksin2\alpha}{\sin^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\alpha}\right|$

$⇒ q^{2} = k^{2}\sin^{2}2\alpha$

$4p^{2} + q^{2} = k^{2} \left(\sin^{2}$2$\alpha + \cos^{2}$2$\alpha\right)

We know that~$\sin^{2}t + \cos^{2}t = 1 .$
$4p^{2} + q^{2} = k^{2}$

$

questions.q: The locus of the mid-points of the perpendiculars drawn from points on the line& $x = 2y$, to the line $x = y$, is.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Slope of $PQ = \dfrac{k - \alpha}{h - 2\alpha} = - 1$
$k - \alpha = - h + 2\alpha$~$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{h + k}{3} \ldots \left(1\right)$
Also,~$2h = 2\alpha + \beta$~and~$2k = \alpha + \beta$
$2h = \alpha +2k⇒ \alpha =2h - 2k \ldots \left(2\right)$
From \left($1\right) & \left(2\right)$,
$\dfrac{h + k}{3} =2 \left(h - k\right)$
So, locus is $6x - 6y = x + y ⇒ 5x = 7y$.

questions.q: Lines are drawn parallel to the line $4x - 3y + 2 = 0,$~at a distance $\dfrac{3}{5}$& units& from the origin. Then which one of the following points lies on any of these lines?
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The equation of a line parallel to the line& $ax + by + c = 0$~is~$ax + by + k = 0 .$

Thus, the equation of a line parallel to $4x - 3y + 2 = 0$~is $4x - 3y + c = 0 .$

The distance of a line~$ax + by + c = 0$~from origin is~\left|c\right|\sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2}} .$

Given the line~$4x - 3y + c = 0$~is~at a distance of $\dfrac{3}{5}$~units from origin

$⇒ \left|c\right|\sqrt{16 + 9} = \dfrac{3}{5}$

$⇒ \left|c\right|5 = \dfrac{3}{5}$

$⇒ c = \pm 3 .$

Hence, the equation of the lines are $4x - 3y + 3 = 0$ and $4x - 3y - 3 = 0 .$

Clearly point \left(- \dfrac{1}{4}, \dfrac{2}{3}\right)$ satisfy the given equation~$4x - 3y + 3 = 0 .

$

questions.q: The number of integral values of $m$~so that the abscissa of point of intersection of lines~$3x + 4y = 9$~and $y = mx + 1$ is also an integer, is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$3x + 4y = 9$

$y = mx + 1$

$⇒ 3x + 4mx + 4 = 9$

$⇒ ( 3 + 4m ) x = 5$

$⇒ x$ will be an integer when

$3 + 4m = 5, - 5, 1, - 1$

$⇒ m = \dfrac{1}{2}, - 2, - \dfrac{1}{2}, - 1$

so, number of integral values of $m$ is $2$

questions.q: The straight lines ${l}_{1}$~and ${l}_{2}$ pass through the origin and trisect the line segment of the line $L: 9x + 5y = 45$ between the axes. If ${m}_{1}$ and ${m}_{2}$ are the slopes of the lines ${l}_{1}$ and ${l}_{2}$,~then the point of intersection of the line $y = ( {m}_{1} + {m}_{2} ) x$ with $L$ lies on
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

The straight lines ${l}_{1}$~and ${l}_{2}$ pass through the origin and trisect the line segment of the line $L: 9x + 5y = 45$ between the axes,

And~${m}_{1}$ and ${m}_{2}$ are the slopes of the lines ${l}_{1}$ and ${l}_{2}$,

Now on plotting the diagram we get,

Given equation of line,~$L: 9x + 5y = 45$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{5} + \dfrac{y}{9} = 1$

Now using the section formula between point~$A \left(5, 0\right) \text{ and } B \left($0, 9\right)$~we get the value of point~$C \text{ and } D$

$⇒ C ≡ $\left(\dfrac{10}{3},$3)$~and~$D ≡ \left(\dfrac{5}{3},6\right)$

Now finding the slope~${m}_{1} \text{ and } {m}_{2}$~we get,

${m}_{1} = \dfrac{3 - 0}{\dfrac{10}{3} - 0} = \dfrac{9}{10} \text{ and } {m}_{2} = \dfrac{6 \times 3}{5} = \dfrac{18}{5}$

So, equation of line~$y = \left({m}_{1} + {m}_{2}\right)x$~will be,

$y = \left(\dfrac{9}{10} + \dfrac{36}{10}\right)x = \dfrac{9}{2}x$

So, intersection point with $L$~will be,

$7y = 45 ⇒ y = \dfrac{45}{7},x = \dfrac{10}{7}$

Hence,~$y - x = \dfrac{45 - 10}{7} =5$

$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given point $B$~lie on the line~$x - y - 2 = 0$, so the point will be~$B \left({x}_{1}, {x}_{1} -2\right)$

Now given distance between $AB$~is \dfrac{29}{3},so by distance formula,

\sqrt{\left({x}_{1} - 4\right)2 + \left({x}_{1} - 2 - 3\right)2} = \dfrac{29}{3}

Now on squaring on both side we get,

$18{x}_{1}^{2} - 162{x}_{1} + 340 = 0$

On solving we get,~${x}_{1} = $\dfrac{51}{9}or~${x}_{1} = $\dfrac{10}{3}

So,~${y}_{1} = $\dfrac{33}{9}~or~${y}_{1} = $\dfrac{4}{3}

Now we can see only~$x + 2y = 6$~will satisfy the point~ \left(\dfrac{10}{3}, \dfrac{4}{3}\right)$

$

questions.q: Let the points  \left(\frac{11}{2}, \alpha\right)$ lie on or inside the triangle with sides $x+y=11, x+2 y=16$ and $2 x+3 y=29$. Then the product of the smallest and the largest values of $\alpha$ is equal to :$

questions.q: If the straight line& $2x - 3y + 17 = 0$ is perpendicular to the line passing through the points  \left(7, 17\right)$ and  \left(15, \beta\right)$, then $\beta$ equals :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Slope of line $2x - 3y + 17 = 0$~is $\dfrac{2}{3}$.

Slope of a line passing~through \left(7, 17\right)$ and \left(15, \beta\right)$~is~$\dfrac{17 - \beta}{7 - 15}$.

Since, both lines are perpendicular to each other, so product of slopes will be~$- 1$.

$⇒ \dfrac{17 - \beta}{7 - 15} \times \dfrac{2}{3} = - 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{17 - \beta}{- 8} = - \dfrac{3}{2} ⇒ 17 - \beta = 12 ⇒ \beta = 5$.

!

questions.q: Let $R$ be the interior region between the lines $3x - y + 1 = 0$ and $x + 2y - 5 = 0$ containing the origin. The set of all values of $a$, for which the points  \left(a^{2}, a + 1\right)$ lie in $R$, is :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let, $P ≡ \left(a^{2}, a + 1\right)$, ${L}_{1}: 3x - y + 1 = 0$ and ${L}_{2}: x + 2y - 5 = 0$.

Now, origin and $P$ lies on the same side with respect to line ${L}_{1}$.

$⇒ {L}_{1} ( 0 ) \cdot {L}_{1} (P ) > 0$

$⇒ 3\left(a^{2}\right) - ( a + 1 ) + 1 > 0$

$⇒ 3a^{2} - a > 0$

$⇒ a\left(3a - 1\right) > 0$

$⇒ a \in ( - \infty ,0 ) \cup \left(\dfrac{1}{3}, \infty\right) . . . \left($i\right)$

Now, ${L}_{2}: x + 2y - 5 = 0$

Origin and $P$ lies on same side with respect to ${L}_{2}$

$⇒ {L}_{2} ( 0 ) $\cdot {L}_{2} ($P ) > 0$

$⇒ a^{2} + 2 ( a + 1 ) - 5 < 0$

$⇒ a^{2} + 2a - 3 < 0$

$⇒ ( a + 3 ) ( a - 1 ) < 0$

$∴ a \in ( - 3, 1 ) . . . \left(ii\right)$

Using intersection of \left($i\right)\text{and}\left($ii\right)$,

$⇒ a \in ( - 3, 0 ) \cup $\left(\dfrac{1}{3},1\right)$

$

Area of~$\Delta ABC = 4 \times \dfrac{1}{2}\left|\dfrac{\left|\begin{\text{ cases }}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{\text{ cases }}\right|2}{{C}_{1}{C}_{2}{C}_{3}}\right|$~

Where~${C}_{1}, {C}_{2}, {C}_{3}$~are cofactors of${c}_{1}, {c}_{2}, {c}_{3}$

$\Delta ABC = 4 \times \dfrac{1}{2}\left|\dfrac{\left|\begin{\text{ cases }}1 & - 1 & 1 \\ 1 & - 2 & 3 \\ 2 & - 5 & 11\end{\text{ cases }}\right|2}{( - 1 ) ( 3 ) ( - 1 )}\right|$

$= 2 \times 9 \div 3$

$= 6$

questions.q: Let the equations of two adjacent sides of a parallelogram& $ABCD$ be $2x - 3y = - 23$~and $5x + 4y = 23$. If the equation of its one diagonal $AC$~is~$3x + 7y = 23$ ~and the distance of~$A$ from the other diagonal is $d$, then~$50d^{2}$ is equal to ______________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

The equations of two adjacent sides of a parallelogram& $ABCD$ be $2x - 3y = - 23$~and $5x + 4y = 23$,

So,~$AB ≡ 2x - 3y = - 23$~and~$BC ≡ 5x + 4y = 23$

Also given,~$AC ≡ 3x + 7y = 23$

Solving the above lines we get,~$A ( – 4, 5 ) , B ( – 1, 7 ) , C ( 3, 2 )$

We know that,

Diagonal of parallelogram have same midpoint,

So~$AC$ and $BD$ have same mid-point~and let point~$D$~be~ \left(x, y\right)$,

So midpoint formula we get,~

$\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{- 4 + 3}{2} ⇒ x = 0$~and~$\dfrac{y + 7}{2} = \dfrac{2 + 5}{2} ⇒ y = 0$

Hence, point~$D$ is~$( 0, 0 )$

Now Equation of $BD$~will be~$7x + y = 0$

Now finding the distance of~$A \left(-4, 5\right)$~from~$7x + y = 0$~we get,

$d = \left|$\dfrac{7 ( - 4 ) + 5}{{7}^{2} + {1}^{2}}\right| = \dfrac{23}{50}

Hence,~$50d^{2} = {23}^{2} = 529$

$

questions.q: If the sum of squares of all real values of $\alpha$, for which the lines $2x - y + 3 = 0, 6x + 3y + 1 = 0$ and $\alpha x + 2y - 2 = 0$ do not form a triangle is $p$, then the greatest integer less than or equal to $p$ is ________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given lines are $2x - y + 3 = 0$, $6x + 3y + 1 = 0$ and $\alpha x + 2y - 2 = 0$.

These lines will not form a triangle if $\alpha x + 2y - 2 = 0$ is concurrent with $2x - y + 3 = 0$ and $6x + 3y + 1 = 0$ or parallel to either of them.

Case-$1$: Concurrent lines

$⇒ \left|$\begin{cases}2 & - 1 & 3 \\ 6 & 3 & 1 \\ \alpha & 2 & - 2\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

$⇒ 2\left(- 6 - 2\right) + 1\left(- 12 - \alpha\right) + 3\left(12 - 3\alpha\right) = 0$

$⇒ - 16 - 12 - \alpha + 36 - 9\alpha = 0$

$⇒ - 10\alpha + 8 = 0$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{4}{5}$

Case-$2$: Parallel lines

$\dfrac{- \alpha}{6} = \dfrac{- 2}{3}$, $- \dfrac{α}{2} = \dfrac{- 2}{- 1}$

$⇒ \alpha = 4$, $\alpha = - 4$

$⇒ P = 16 + 16 + \dfrac{16}{25}$

$[ P ] = \left[32 + \dfrac{16}{25}\right] = 32$

questions.q: A ray of light passing through the point $P  \left(2, 3\right)$~reflects on the $X$-axis at point $A$ and the reflected ray passes through the point $Q  \left(5, 4\right)$. questions.solution:
By observation we know the point& $A \left(\alpha,0\right)$~and~$\beta =y$-coordinate of~$R= $\dfrac{2 \times 4 + 1 \times 0}{2 + 1} = \dfrac{8}{3}$⋯ \left(1\right)$

Now~$P^{'}$~is image of~$P$~in~$y = 0$~which will be~$P^{'} \left(2, - 3\right)$

$∴$~ Equation of~$P^{'}Q$~is~ \left($y + 3\right) = \dfrac{4 + 3}{5 - 2}\left(x - 2\right)$~

i.e.~$3y + 9 = 7x - 14$

Now~$P^{'}Q$~meets~$x -$axis at~$A$

so~$A ≡ \left(\dfrac{23}{7},$0\right)$~by solving with~$y = 0$

$∴ $\alpha = \dfrac{23}{7}$⋯ \left($2\right)$

By~ \left(1\right), \left($2\right)$, we get

7\alpha ++3\beta =23 + 8 = 31$

$

questions.q: A triangle is formed by $X$-axis, $Y$-axis and the line $3x + 4y = 60$. Then the number of points $P  \left(a, b\right)$~which lie strictly inside the triangle, where $a$~is an integer and $b$ is a multiple of $a, is _____ .$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:
